newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks pause advance in mild correction.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks pause advance in mild correction.

text.p: Greek equities took a breather after a six-day rally in a mild correction. Stoks emerged softer and struggled their way back intrasession to close lower after profit taking. Trading volume was moderate and sentiment remained bullish, brokers said.

"We had a correction which was due after the runup, a logical reaction which may leave the market fluctuating around 940 points with trading on the heavy side," said broker Yannis Kalogerakis at ABN Axias Securities.
"The market will stay on its upternd, and prices will resume their move to the upside soon."
Brokers said sentiment remained bullish on expectations that snap polls will bring about a strong government that will steer the economy harder towards its EMU goal.

"The stock market will consolidate its gains this week. We expect overall sentiment to remain positive throughout the short pre-election period in anticipation of a stable and market friendly government," said Telesis Securities in a report.

The Athens general share index closed 0.25 percent, or 2.33 points lower at 946.25 from Monday's 948.58 close after opening at 945.47 points. Turnover dropped to 8.84 billion drachmas on volume of 4.6 million shares.
Last Friday Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos signed a decree ordering the dissolution of the 300-seat parliament ahead of early elections on September 22.

Gainers trailed losers 85 to 130 with 24 issues unchanged on 239 traded. Banks closed flat, industrials ended 0.44 percent lower with construction rising 0.29 percent. Small-caps slid 0.38 percent to 81.75 on the parallel market index.
